leads.title: Zavala Family Inc. v. Superior Court (Cal. Ct. App., 2nd Dist., Div. 8, No. B352255, certified for publication, decided Nov. 24, 2026) -- published opinion holds LA Metro may pursue unlawful detainer against a condemned commercial tenant instead of a separate eminent-domain possession proceeding
leads.why: Fresh (decided yesterday), certified-for-publication precedent on the eminent domain/unlawful detainer intersection. LA County Metropolitan Transportation Authority acquired, under threat of condemnation, property leased by Zavala Family Inc. (and Jose Zavala individually -- the newsroom should name only the business entity per CLAUDE.md's no-individuals rule) to run a scrap-metal recycling business; when the business stayed on after acquisition, Metro brought an unlawful detainer action rather than a separate eminent-domain possession proceeding. The Court of Appeal held the UD action may proceed and denied the writ petition. No dollar figure stated in the opinion excerpt reviewed; matters to any commercial tenant facing a public-agency taking.

leads.title: One Wailea Development LLC v. Maui Planning Commission (Haw. ICA, No. CAAP-24-0000649, summary disposition order, Nov. 24, 2026) -- appeals court affirms revocation of developer's Special Management Area permit and sanctions for frivolous appeal
leads.why: Fresh (decided yesterday) land-use dispute: the Maui Planning Commission terminated a Special Management Area Use Permit it had granted developer One Wailea Development LLC in 1999; the circuit court affirmed the termination and granted the Commission's motion for sanctions against the developer for a frivolous appeal, and the ICA affirmed both. Real developer and government-agency parties, real court, real outcome (permit revocation plus sanctions) -- moderate significance but clearly commercial real estate on its face.

leads.title: Torres v. 120 Broadway Holdings, LLC (N.Y. App. Div., 1st Dept., decided Nov. 24, 2026, Index No. 159374/18) -- appeals court grants partial summary judgment to injured worker in Labor Law suit over gut renovation at Silverstein Properties-managed 120 Broadway
leads.why: Fresh (decided yesterday) construction/premises matter naming a major NYC commercial owner-manager: during a Silverstein Properties-managed gut renovation at 120 Broadway in Manhattan, a ceiling-collapse injury case under Labor Law. The Appellate Division modified the lower court, granting plaintiff summary judgment on the Labor Law section 241(6) claim, dismissing claims against demolition subcontractor Rite-Way, and denying defendants summary judgment on the remaining claims. No damages figure yet (liability phase only) -- fits the site's construction-defect/premises-liability categories and names Silverstein Properties, Inc., JRM Construction Management LLC and Rite-Way Internal Removal, Inc. as parties.
